request.system: You are an expert in clinical classification systems.

messages.content:
ICD-10-AM is the Australian modification of the International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, 10th revision. Its disease codes are arranged in chapters, and a three-character category is written as one capital letter followed by two digits. The letter indicates the chapter or block: A and B are infectious diseases, C is malignant neoplasms, D is other neoplasms and blood disorders, E is endocrine, nutritional and metabolic disease, F is mental and behavioural disorders, G is the nervous system, H is the eye and ear, I is the circulatory system, J is the respiratory system, K is the digestive system, L is the skin, M is the musculoskeletal system, N is the genitourinary system, O is pregnancy and childbirth, P is the perinatal period, Q is congenital malformations, R is symptoms and abnormal findings, S and T are injury and poisoning, and Z is factors influencing health status. The two digits narrow the chapter to a specific category, for example J44 is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and N17 is acute kidney failure.

The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Using that structure, assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. Choose the chapter letter first, then the two digits.

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary:

Patient: 42-year-old female with a past medical history of rheumatoid arthritis

Hospital Course:

The patient was admitted due to psychomotor agitation and neutrophilia. The lumbar puncture showed a low glucose level in the cerebrospinal fluid and common germs in FilmArray despite negative Gram and Chinese ink. The patient was initiated on antibiotic therapy, antituberculosis drugs, and antifungal agents. The patient showed some improvements three days after initiating treatment but then presented a new episode of altered mental status, which was associated with transaminase elevation. Brain CT scan revealed ischemic areas in the corpus callosum and bilateral parietal lobes. The patient presented severe hemodynamic decompensation with metabolic acidosis, acute respiratory failure, and pancytopenia one day later, which required the transfer to the MICU. The autoimmune markers were requested due to the suspicion of immune alveolar hemorrhage, and the patient met the CAPS criteria. The patient was initiated on intravenous pulses of methylprednisolone 1 g daily IV and enoxaparin 60 mg daily SubQ. Despite the initial clinical improvement, the patient passed away due to new respiratory, renal, and encephalopathic deterioration in later days.
Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Discharge Condition:

The patient passed away due to new respiratory, renal, and encephalopathic deterioration.

Discharge Instructions:

None. This patient did not survive. 

Follow-Up Care:

None. This patient did not survive. 

Signed,

[Physician's Name]

Answer in the form CODE: <letter><digit><digit>

text:
CODE: D68

The episode was chiefly due to catastrophic antiphospholipid syndrome (CAPS), which the team confirmed by meeting its criteria. That condition is classified under antiphospholipid syndrome (D68.61) in the D68 category, a blood disorder involving an immune mechanism.
